name: Petronas Towers
headline: height
subtitle: Height of each of the two identical towers
description: The Petronas Towers are two identical 88-storey towers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, completed in 1998 and linked by a skybridge at the 41st and 42nd floors. The Skyscraper Center lists each tower at 451.9 m (1,483 ft), both to the architectural top and to the tip. They shared the title of world's tallest building from 1998 until Taipei 101 overtook them in 2004, and they remain the tallest twin towers in the world.

facts.text: Each tower has 88 floors above ground and 5 below ground; construction started in 1992 and finished in 1998.
They are the tallest twin towers in the world and shared the title of world's tallest building from 1998 to 2004, between the Sears Tower and Taipei 101.
The skybridge at the 41st and 42nd floors gives no structural benefit, but lets the towers share facilities and is part of the fire evacuation plan.
Two construction consortiums, one Japanese and one South Korean, each built one tower; Tower 2 reached its top first.
The design is based on Islamic geometry, reflecting Malaysia's cultural heritage.

caveats: The Skyscraper Center database now carries the Council on Vertical Urbanism (CVU) name; its height categories are the CTBUH ones (architectural top includes spires but not antennas).
The Skyscraper Center lists the two towers separately; Tower 1 and Tower 2 have identical heights and floor counts.
The distance between the two towers was not sourced, so only one tower's height is given.
World rankings change as new towers are completed; the ranks quoted are as shown on the Skyscraper Center in September 2026.
